title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
quote: In the flies with unilateral expression, we found that light evoked a small average steering bias in the ipsilateral direction
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv, and its line SS00730 maps only to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm light from above the head, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: line typically drives expression in one DN per hemisphere; this record is the unilateral-expression group
sensory_condition: walking on spherical treadmill; head cuticle intact; symmetric illumination from above
other_cell_types: specific optic lobe cell types (unnamed; Fig. S8A legend)
specific VNC cell types (unnamed; Fig. S8A legend)
penetrance: small average ipsilateral steering bias; mean outside the 95% CI of the bilateral-control bootstrap (Fig. 8B-C)
n_flies_note: Methods: left-only expression in 9 and right-only in 8 brains; Fig. 8B legend reads 'mean of 16/17 flies (uni/bilateral ReaChR)'
notes: Flies were walking on the ball when stimulated, so legs are not_assessed (convention: turning in already-walking flies). Expression was produced stochastically by hs-FLP and scored post hoc. Adjudicated field: line_specificity.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior' (data not shown); Fig. 8B-C bilateral group
quote: These effects were likely due to visual startle, because they were indistinguishable in flies with unilateral expression, bilateral expression, and no expression
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv, and its line SS00730 maps only to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm light from above the head, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: line typically drives expression in one DN per hemisphere; this record is the bilateral-expression group
sensory_condition: walking on spherical treadmill; head cuticle intact; symmetric illumination from above
other_cell_types: specific optic lobe cell types (unnamed; Fig. S8A legend)
specific VNC cell types (unnamed; Fig. S8A legend)
penetrance: forward-velocity changes indistinguishable from unilateral- and no-expression flies (data not shown); bilateral group rotational velocity centred on 0 (Fig. 8C)

notes: The authors attribute forward-velocity changes to visual startle and say they could not use this dataset to assess DNa02's effect on forward velocity. Adjudicated field: line_specificity.

title: Hierarchical Transformation of Navigational Variables into Coordinated Turning
source_locator: Supplementary Video 6 legend (Supplementary Information p. 2); Results 'DNa11 controls all six legs'
quote: We found however that unilateral DNa11 activation is still capable of eliciting turning in decapitated flies, albeit much more slowly
mapping_basis: DNa11 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv (hemibrain VES008); SS77821 is not in the kit, but the paper's Supplementary Table 1 lists 'DNa11-SS: SS77821'.
stimulation: 660 nm red light (setup as for SPARC experiments); exact parameters for decapitated flies not separately stated
type_coverage: single DNa11 neuron labelled (unilateral, stochastic SPARC2-D)
sensory_condition: decapitated; tethered; filmed from ipsilateral and contralateral sides
penetrance: 8/8 decapitated flies examined turned towards the ipsilateral side
notes: The substrate for decapitated flies is not stated (Methods describe no decapitation protocol), so headless_surface is 'other'. Supplementary Video 6 was not downloaded. The text gives no leg kinematics, step counts or baseline state for headless flies. Sex is inferred from Methods ('In most of the experiments, only females were used'; no exception stated for SPARC). Adjudicated fields: front/middle/hind_leg_rhythm.

title: Hierarchical Transformation of Navigational Variables into Coordinated Turning
quote: We found that all four descending neurons elicited ipsilateral turns during walking, albeit with widely varying potency (Fig. 2c and Fig. S3)
mapping_basis: DNa03 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv; SS84990 is not in the kit, but the paper's Supplementary Table 1 lists 'DNa03-SS2: SS84990'.
stimulation: 660 nm laser via fibre, ~0.73 mW/mm2, 5 s constant light
sensory_condition: walking on spherical treadmill, very dim ambient light
other_cell_types: optic lobe neurons (unnamed; visible in Fig. S1f)
other central brain and VNC cells (unnamed; visible in Fig. S1f)
penetrance: DNa03 turns of smaller amplitude and lower penetrance than DNa11 (Fig. 2c, Fig. S3)
notes: Fig. S3 groups flies by left, right, both or neither neuron labelled; the main-text quote covers DNa03 generally (Fig. 2c uses DNa03-SS1). Adjudicated field: line_specificity.

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
quote: Activation drove consistent increases in forward walking speed, leading to longer walking trajectories during the period of red light exposure
mapping_basis: The kit maps the name DNp17 and line SS02553 to two MANC types, DNp17 and DNut046. The paper's anatomy (6 neurons per hemisphere; lower tectulum, haltere and neck neuropils) does not pick one, so UNMAPPED per section 4.
stimulation: 625 nm LED ring, 0.41-4.07 mW/cm2 (5 intensities), 10 s pulses, 9 cycles per intensity
sensory_condition: UFO arena, groups of up to 20 flies, white background light 0.11 mW/cm2
other_cell_types: DopaMeander (neuron type 2, dopaminergic local brain interneuron)
penetrance: significantly faster forward walking than empty controls across intensities; increased tortuosity
notes: Increased locomotion scored by centroid tracking without leg tracking, so confidence is at most medium. The paper attributes the phenotype to DopaMeander (a non-DN in the line), not DNp17 (Fig. 3; Discussion). The 'minor_offtarget' label understates that the off-target cell drives the phenotype. Adjudicated field: manc_type.

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 3D-F (DNp17>CsChr without DopaMeander, blue); Discussion 'DNp17 is unlikely to drive fast forward walking'
quote: DNp17 increases walking speed only slightly, if at all, but that DopaMeander labeling is much more predictive of forward walking
mapping_basis: The kit maps the name DNp17 and line SS02553 to two MANC types, DNp17 and DNut046. The paper's anatomy (6 neurons per hemisphere; lower tectulum, haltere and neck neuropils) does not pick one, so UNMAPPED per section 4.
stimulation: 625 nm LED ring, 4.07 mW/cm2, 10 s pulses, 9 trials
type_coverage: stochastic subset of SS02553 neurons including DNp17 but not DopaMeander
other_cell_types: possible co-labelling of SS02553 neuron types 3-8 (local brain interneurons, ascending neurons, VNC local neuron); DopaMeander excluded in this group
penetrance: small speed increase (~2-3 mm/s in Fig. 3E), significantly less than flies with DopaMeander (p=0.006)
n_flies_note: approximately 6-7 flies (blue dots, Fig. 3E); not stated in text
notes: Legs are unclear: the authors say DNp17 raises speed 'only slightly, if at all', there is no test against no-expression flies for this group, and other SS02553 types may be co-labelled. No leg tracking. Adjudicated field: manc_type.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. S1-1C; Fig. S2-1A-B, G-H; Fig. S2-2I; Supplemental Table 2 (DNp07_2); Video S2
quote: DNp07, DNp10, DNp47, and DNg79 drive extensions of all six legs as part of the landing response
mapping_basis: DNp07 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv, and SS02612 (the paper's 'DNp07_2') maps to DNp07 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 150 uW/mm2, 50 ms pulses, 10 s inter-stimulus interval
coordination_notes: extension of all six legs (landing response)
n_flies_note: Supplemental Table 2: N=8 flies, n=32 trials
notes: Leg extension is a single movement, so legs are 'no'. Tarsal tips were tracked with DeepLabCut. The paper's own LPLC4 simulation and ShREC metric are not Pugliese-type scores. Adjudicated field: line_specificity.

title: Neurons Underlying Aggression-Like Actions That Are Shared by Both Males and Females in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'Activation of L320 neurons drives multiple aggressive behaviors'; Figs. 1, 3, 4, 5; Fig. 6 (anatomy)
quote: drives multiple aggressive actions including wing threat, wing extension, and thrusting, as well as holding an alert posture in both isolated male and female flies
mapping_basis: The paper found no hemibrain DN matching the L320 DN and did not search further; the kit has no entry for L320.
stimulation: 617 nm red light, 8.9 mW/cm2, 15 s per trial, 15 trials per fly
sensory_condition: isolated fly in 20x10x10 mm chamber, IR illumination, enclosed in dark box
penetrance: variable across trials and flies; wing threat absent in all trials of one fly (Fig. 4A)
n_flies_note: 12 female + 11 male retinal-fed flies, 15 trials each
notes: Legs were not tracked. Front legs are described only in single movements: lifted then snapped down in thrusts, and straightened in the alert stance (Fig. 3; Results). Middle and hind legs are not described beyond sometimes leaving the ground during thrusts. Retreat was observed but not quantified. The paper attributes the behaviour to CL062, not the DN (Figs. 7, 9, 10). Adjudicated fields: front/middle/hind_leg_rhythm.

title: Neurons Underlying Aggression-Like Actions That Are Shared by Both Males and Females in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 7C; Fig. 9A (spatially targeted DMD activation of the DN region)
quote: We found that activation of the CL062 axons, but not the other neurons, drove a robust increase in wingspan (Figs. 7C, 9A).
mapping_basis: The paper found no hemibrain DN matching the L320 DN and did not search further; the kit has no entry for L320.
stimulation: 617 nm light, 2 mW/cm2, DMD spot restricted to the DN, delivered at the neuron focal plane
sensory_condition: head-fixed, posterior head cuticle removed, on air-supported ball; light spatially restricted by DMD
penetrance: no wingspan increase when the DN was targeted
notes: Only wingspan and wing pitch were quantified; legs are not described. DMD targeting restricts light, not expression; the authors report spill-over activation of nearby neurons in this preparation (Results, Fig. 7C). Adjudicated field: line_specificity.

title: Whole-body 3D kinematics of freely behaving Drosophila
source_locator: Section 2.5; Fig. 5c-d; Supplementary Video 5 legend; Methods 'Fly husbandry and behavioral experiments'
quote: Illuminating the arena with a red LED reliably elicited sustained running bouts, which we tracked with a modified headless skeleton
mapping_basis: DNg100 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv (literature synonym BDN2), and VT058557-AD;R85F12-DBD is listed as DNg100 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: red LED flashlight (intensity not stated); arena also lit by strobed white LEDs, which the authors say also activate CsChrimson
sensory_condition: decapitated, freely moving in a 24x5.5x9.5 mm chamber under strobed white light
coordination_notes: running step cycles fall within the wild-type PC space; reduced tibia and femur flexion (Fig. 5c-d)
penetrance: red LED 'reliably elicited sustained running bouts'; Supplementary Video 5: fly speeds up when red light turns on
n_flies_note: not stated; 50 speed-matched running cycles analysed (Fig. 5d)
notes: The white strobe light also activates CsChrimson (Discussion), so the headless fly was probably already being driven before the red light. The red light increased speed (Supplementary Video 5 legend). 3D leg tracking shows running step cycles. Adjudicated field: effect_on_walking.
